mode achieved: static design review only. Read the brief, spec sections 3, 5.5 and 9, the seven root configs, every shipped file of src/core, src/platform and src/mocks, five route files, the shell core (model, Shell, useShell, locale, NotBuilt, strings, two test helpers), screen 24 (Screen, model, model.tools, model.lists head, useOverview, StateView, strings, contract.yaml), 24 design-system files, six gate scripts and both custom lint rules; ran ponytail:ponytail-review (resolved, folded into the findings) and six static scans (python3 and grep). No Jest, ESLint, tsc, Stryker, Playwright or expo command was run: Stryker run in progress.
verdict: NEEDS-WORK. Worth keeping: tokens have one source (brand/tokens.css, gen-tokens.mjs, gate:tokens; e2e reads tokens.css at run time, e2e/web/support.ts:7-16); the shipped components I read take every label from a dictionary or a model built from one; model.ts is pure; contract.yaml drives e2e and the trace gate; the gate scripts and both custom lint rules encode spec rules I found no off-the-shelf tool for, and serve-web.mjs is not reinvention (expo serve has no single-page fallback, node_modules/@expo/cli/build/src/serve/serveAsync.js:133-160). Ponytail net: about -15 lines and -4 files from the forks, up to -42 files from the styles merge.
🔴 blocker  Fixture ids and names are retyped by hand in tests, e2e, the mock server, shipped config and the release check
- key: src/mocks/fixtures#restated-fixture-ids
- Where: src/mocks/handlers.ts:11-22 (BASE, WORKSPACE, both Map key lists and FORBIDDEN restate fixtures/shell.ts:34-57 and platform/config.ts:4); src/platform/config.ts:8 and config.test.ts:4,8; scripts/check-web-release.mjs:14-17; src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.helper.tsx:3 vs 17-19 (imports `meridian`, then types 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh', 'creative-studio', 'meridian-cgi-campaign' instead of `meridian.timeZone`); src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:11-17; e2e/web/shape.spec.ts:6, controls.spec.ts:10, brand.spec.ts:9 (the Meridian overview path is defined on 13 lines).
- Why: Measured (a quoted literal equal to a string value of src/mocks/fixtures/*.ts, in *.test.*, *.spec.* and test helpers): 339 lines in 53 files; eight ids and names alone ('creative-studio' 55, 'meridian-cgi-campaign' 49, 'Creative Studio' 18, 'Nadia R.' 15, 'Meridian CGI Campaign' 11, 'spring-catalogue-renders' 9, 'northwind-showroom-vr' 9, 'Northwind Furniture Co.' 9) occur 175 times; 158 test lines in 46 files hand-type route paths. Mechanism: the fixtures export whole objects but no named ids (a project id lives only deep in `creativeStudio.tree[0].programs[0].projects[0].id` and as Map keys), so even the mock server restates them; plan B's code blocks carried the literals (`workspaceId: 'creative-studio',` 30 times in plan/2026-10-06-frontend-overview-screen.md, `const MERIDIAN = [` at its line 13121) and agents copied them; there is no shared test kit and no rule. Multiplier: one screen produced 175 copies of eight values; each plan C screen brings its own test files and e2e specs with the same habit (50 screens), and every fixture rename becomes a repo-wide search.
- Fix: one `src/mocks/fixtures/ids.ts` (`export const IDS = { workspace: 'creative-studio', otherWorkspace: 'digital-products', meridian: 'meridian-cgi-campaign', showroom: 'northwind-showroom-vr', forbidden: 'spring-catalogue-renders' } as const`) read by the shell.ts tree and by handlers.ts (`new Map([[IDS.meridian, meridian], [IDS.showroom, showroom]])`, `FORBIDDEN = IDS.forbidden`, BASE built from `apiConfig.baseUrl`); tests read IDS and fixture fields (`crumbsOf(creativeStudio, IDS.meridian)` instead of MERIDIAN, `meridian.timeZone`); one `e2e/web/paths.ts` builds the 13 path constants from IDS (e2e already imports src, e2e/web/links.ts:3-5); check-web-release.mjs derives its fixture markers from the fixture files at run time; HOME stays a literal (shipped code may not import src/mocks, eslint.config.js:155-159) but config.test.ts:8 asserts that HOME's ids exist in `creativeStudio.tree` instead of restating them. Guard: the restated-literal lint rule of the next finding.
- approach-changing: no, one module and a mechanical rewrite; it does change the test template plan C copies.
- trigger: rename the demo project id or client in src/mocks/fixtures/shell.ts:51 or meridian.ts:12; state: handlers.ts:19-20, config.ts:8, the 13 e2e path constants, check-web-release.mjs:14 and 53 test files keep the old literal; outcome: the renamed project's sidebar link opens "Project not found" in the dev and e2e builds (handlers.ts:83-84 finds no body), tests fail across unrelated files, and the release check keeps searching for a string that no longer exists, so that marker silently guards nothing.
- guard-bypass: nothing types the Map keys or HOME against the shell tree (plain string literals), no lint rule or gate looks at literals in test files, and scripts/check-web-release.test.mjs restates the same marker strings, so it stays green when the fixtures change and the markers do not.
- design: yes, a fixture-ids module, an e2e paths module and a restated-literal lint rule for test files.
🟡 major  UI copy is retyped in tests beside the dictionaries, with two conventions side by side
- key: src/**/strings#copy-restated-in-tests
- Where: src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:25 and 31 (`strings={STRINGS.en}` next to a hand-typed `label: 'Open menu'`); heaviest files src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.test.native.tsx (43 lines), model.test.ts (43), src/shell/model.sidebar.test.ts (29), Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx (27), Sidebar.test.native.tsx (20).
- Why: Measured (a quoted literal equal to an en.ts value of 4 or more characters, in test, spec and helper files; an upper bound, since titles that quote a label count too): 495 lines in 58 files ('Language' 17, 'Overview' 16, 'Open menu' 15, 'Workspaces' 14, 'Not built yet' 14), while 24 test files already derive copy from STRINGS. The shipped side is clean (Shell.tsx, NotBuilt.tsx, Screen.tsx, StateView.tsx read every label from a dictionary), so the dictionary is the source of truth and the tests are the drift. Spec 5.5:317 makes copy edits a planned event (the owner approves the wording at screen review), and each edit is now a hunt through test files; with two conventions in the code, plan C developers copy whichever file they open first.
- Fix: tests name copy by key (`getByLabelText(STRINGS.en.menu.open)`, STRINGS.vi for the vi locale); if the owner wants the wireframe wording pinned, one test per dictionary pins en.ts to it. Guard: one ESLint rule in eslint-rules/ (about 40 lines) for `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.test.helper.*` and `e2e/**` that loads the string values of `src/**/strings/{en,vi}.ts` and `src/mocks/fixtures/*.ts` by regex and reports any equal string literal, with a `// restated-literal: <reason>` escape modeled on `token-exception:` (eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js:7, 92-100).
- approach-changing: no, a lint rule and a mechanical rewrite.
- trigger: the owner changes 'Open menu' in src/shell/strings/en.ts:13 at screen review; state: 15 test lines type 'Open menu'; outcome: the tests that query the old label fail in unrelated files, each is fixed by retyping the new literal, and the next copy edit repeats the hunt.
- guard-bypass: the only copy rule (eslint.config.js:80-100) covers shipped src/design-system/**/*.tsx and ignores tests; nothing else compares test literals with the dictionaries.
- design: yes, the restated-literal lint rule (shared with the fixture finding).
🔴 blocker  Comments, test titles, lint messages and tool output are in Vietnamese and cite rulings that live only in 1.4 MB of Vietnamese plans; no convention or guard exists
- key: apps/metis#code-language-and-ruling-ids
- Where: every layer; examples src/core/api/client.ts:6 (`// Named errors the screen knows how to draw (spec 3.3, 4.5, R-B15)...`), src/shell/Shell.tsx:76-77 (D-B22, D-B23), src/design-system/Select.styles.ts:40-46 (a 7-line measurement log in a style file), scripts/verify.mjs:32 ('green' / 'RED'), eslint.config.js:22-164 (every lint message), eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js:85-87, src/screens/24-project-overview/strings/strings.test.ts:7 (test title).
- Why: Measured with a diacritics scan over apps/metis (ts, tsx, js, mjs, cjs, json, jsonc, yaml, html; build output excluded): comments in shipped code, config and scripts 808 lines in 170 files; comments in tests 556 lines in 100 files; test titles 489 lines in 105 files; lint, tool and error messages 75 lines in 17 files; test data and assertion strings 190 lines in 45 files (partly legitimate vi-locale data); the two vi dictionaries 137 lines (legitimate). Comments citing ruling ids, spec sections or plan tasks: 214 lines (167 in shipped code) in 140 files; they resolve only inside plan/ (plan B 941 KB, 1.4 MB in total, Vietnamese). Mechanism: agents copied plan code blocks verbatim (the client.ts:6 comment appears word for word in plan/2026-10-05-frontend-foundation.md and plan/2026-10-06-frontend-overview-screen.md), and nothing said otherwise: apps/metis has no README or CONTRIBUTING, and the only rules sit in the git-excluded local CLAUDE.md. Multiplier: every file plan C writes copies the style; a 40-person agency cannot read the why of any decision, so it will delete or contradict it.
- Fix: commit a one-page apps/metis/CONTRIBUTING.md in English: English for code, comments, test titles, tool output and lint messages; Vietnamese only in `**/strings/vi.ts`, `NATIVE_NAMES` (src/core/i18n/locale.ts:10) and vi-locale tests that read STRINGS.vi; a comment gives the why in one English line, with no ruling ids, spec numbers, dates or device measurements (those belong in the commit message or the plan). Example: client.ts:6 becomes `// Every failure becomes a typed ApiError the screen can render; the client never throws.` Guard: `eslint-rules/english-only.js`, about 25 lines in the shape of eslint-rules/stryker-disable-reason.js:15-24 (which already scans every comment in Program()), reporting Vietnamese diacritics in comments and string literals outside that allowlist, and `R-[A-Z]\d+|D-B\d+|FE-\d+` in comments; gate:lint (`eslint .`, package.json:70) already reaches src, e2e, scripts and eslint-rules; add a canary entry; translate the lint messages first and keep canary.mjs:135 (`expect: 'spec 5.5'`, a substring of the message at eslint.config.js:90) in step. Test titles keep their requirement codes for scripts/check-trace.mjs:54-57.
- approach-changing: no, a convention, one lint rule and a mechanical translation before plan C.
- trigger: an agency developer or a plan C agent opens any of the 288 files; state: the why is a Vietnamese sentence citing R-B15 or D-B22; outcome: they cannot verify or preserve the decision, and their new file copies the same style because nothing rejects it.
- guard-bypass: no lint rule, gate or committed document covers language or ruling ids; the comment rules in gate:lint cover only disable directives (eslint-comments recommended plus require-description) and Stryker directives (stryker-disable-reason).
- design: yes, a committed convention document plus an english-only lint rule with a canary.
🟡 major  Screen-generic machinery lives inside screen 24, and the lint row that forbids importing another screen turns screen 25 into a copy
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview#screen-kit-trapped
- Where: useOverview.ts:9-29 (the stale-answer guard, already a second copy of src/shell/useShell.ts:11-25); model.ts:137-175 (problemOf, ApiError to screen state); states/StateView.tsx:1-88 (typed from `../model` at lines 9 and 12) with StateView.test.native.tsx (190 lines); model.tools.ts:20-36 (num, counted, ids, wbs); strings/en.ts:111-138 and vi.ts (generic state copy: session expired, invalid data, retry, back); eslint.config.js:160-165 (per-screen zone).
- Why: About 260 shipped lines of screen 24 (plus StateView.test.native.tsx and useOverview.test.native.ts, 292 test lines) are not about the overview: every data screen needs the fetch hook, the 401/403/404/invalid/unavailable mapping, the state view and the plural helper. Spec 5.5:309 forbids merging dictionaries between screens and the per-screen lint zone forbids importing screen 24, so plan C's path of least resistance is to copy the files with their tests. Multiplier: 50 screens; a fix to the stale-answer guard or the session-expired flow then lands 50 times, and coverage and mutation pass on every copy.
- Fix: before screen 25, move the generic part to a layer every screen may import: one `useApi(key, fetcher)` hook replacing the bodies of useShell and useOverview; problemOf, StateView and a shared `states` copy block in src/shell (Screen.tsx:6-9 already imports four shell modules and the shell dictionary exists); `num` and `counted` beside interpolate in src/core/i18n. The screen keeps only its own wording ("Could not load the project overview"). Name the trade-off in spec 3.1: src/shell becomes the screens' kit, a role the layout does not state today.
- approach-changing: yes, it changes the screen template and the folder roles plan C copies.
- trigger: plan C starts screen 26 (WBS); state: the generic pieces exist only in src/screens/24-project-overview and eslint.config.js:160-165 rejects importing them; outcome: the developer copies useOverview.ts, problemOf, StateView.tsx with its 190-line test and the states copy in two languages, and the template now carries two diverging copies.
- guard-bypass: the gates reward the copy (coverage and mutation pass on duplicated code, knip sees both copies as used), and no rule looks for duplicated modules.
- design: yes, a named shared location for the screen kit (data hook, state mapping, state view, state copy) recorded in spec 3.1.
🟡 major  The project header is typed by the overview contract and always marks Overview active
- key: src/shell/model.ts#project-header-coupled-to-overview
- Where: src/shell/model.ts:152-156 (TABS lists six project tabs; `projectHeaderOf(project: Overview['project'], ...)`) and :187 (`active: key === 'overview'`); src/core/api/overview.ts:43-56 (header data exists only in GET .../overview); src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.tsx:30 (the only caller).
- Why: Charter, WBS, Plan, Governance and Focus are the next project tabs; each must draw the same header with its own active tab, but the header's input type is the overview response and its active tab is a constant. Plan C must then fetch the overview on every tab (two calls per page, and a back-end contract other screens depend on) or fork projectHeaderOf. The comment at model.ts:154-155 records the assumption ("only the overview draws the header") that plan C breaks.
- Fix: `projectHeaderOf(project: ProjectHeaderData, active: Destination, c)` with `ProjectHeaderData` its own zod schema in src/core/api, embedded by every project contract or served once (with the shell or its own endpoint; a back-end contract decision to record in spec 3.5); then `active: key === active`.
- approach-changing: yes, it decides the API contract shape every project screen shares.
- trigger: plan C builds the Charter tab; state: projectHeaderOf accepts only `Overview['project']` and hard-codes Overview as active; outcome: Charter either calls the overview endpoint for its header or renders a header that highlights Overview on the Charter page.
- guard-bypass: one caller today, so no type error or test fails; the header tests feed the overview fixture (src/shell/ProjectHeader.test.helper.tsx:10-21), which is the coupling itself.
- design: yes, a shared project-header contract and an active-tab parameter.
🟡 major  Boundary lint follows spec 3.2 to the letter but leaves three bypasses, and two of the four rows have no canary
- key: eslint.config.js#boundary-bypasses
- Where: eslint.config.js:171-182 (no-restricted-imports names only react, react-native and react-dom), :139-143 and :160-165 (a screen's model.ts may import anything in its own folder), :180 (no-restricted-globals); scripts/canary.mjs:61-78 (canaries for rows 1 and 2 only).
- Why: Row-by-row reading of the config (static, no lint run): row 1, core to UI layers, configured at 110-120, canaried; row 1, core and models to react and react-native, configured at 171-181 for those package names only, so a value import of expo-router, expo-*, react-native-* or @react-native-picker/* in src/core or a model.ts is not covered; row 1, models to UI layers, configured at 121-143, except that a screen model may import its own Screen.tsx, blocks/*, states/* and useOverview.ts (the zone at 139-143 excludes src/screens models by construction and the per-screen zone exempts the own folder); row 1, globals, configured at 180 for bare window, document and localStorage, while `globalThis.localStorage` is [Unverified - confirm before applying]; row 2, design-system, configured at 144-154, canaried; row 3, screen to screen, configured at 160-165, vacuous with one screen, no canary; row 4, mocks, configured at 117, 150 and 155-159 for core, design-system, shell, screens and app, no canary. The spec row is itself contradictory (it forbids every model.ts from importing src/screens/, spec line 115, while the screen model must read its own strings, line 100); the config resolved it silently by exempting screen models. Probe for the model bypass: add `src/screens/24-project-overview/model.canary.ts` containing `import { HealthCard } from './blocks/HealthCard'` and `export const x = HealthCard`, then run `pnpm gate:lint`; expected from the config: no error. NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress.
- Fix: add patterns `['expo', 'expo-*', '@expo/*', 'react-native-*', '@react-native*/*', 'msw', 'msw/*']` to the block at eslint.config.js:176-179; in the same block (model files only) reject relative imports other than `./model.*` and `./strings` (exact pattern syntax to confirm with the probe above); add two canaries (a screen importing another screen, a shell file importing src/mocks) beside canary.mjs:61-78; amend spec 3.2 row 1 to "outside its own model.* and strings/".
- approach-changing: no, configuration plus two canaries.
- trigger: a developer adds a value import of `router` from expo-router to src/core/routes.ts, or makes screen 24's model.ts import `./blocks/HealthCard`; state: eslint.config.js as is; outcome: gate:lint passes and the pure TypeScript layer now loads React, so spec 3.2's promise (core reusable by a back-end, models testable in Node) breaks silently.
- guard-bypass: the restricted-imports list names two packages rather than the UI ecosystem, the zones exempt a screen's own folder, and no canary exercises rows 3 and 4 or the model rule.
- design: yes, two canaries and an import pattern set for core and model files.
💭 nit  Release configuration hard-wires the mock host and the demo project, with no environment seam
- key: src/platform/config.ts#release-config-is-mock-data
- Where: src/platform/config.ts:4 (`baseUrl: 'https://api.metis.test'`, a host that never resolves, also in release builds) and :8 (HOME, two fixture ids); used by src/app/index.tsx:8 (root redirect) and src/shell/Shell.tsx:82 (the shell of every page outside a workspace); pinned by src/platform/config.test.ts:4,8.
- Why: intended for plan B, where only mocks exist, but there is no seam: a real API means editing shipped code and a test that pins the literals, and against real data /me/... and /search would load the shell of a workspace that does not exist ("Could not load the menu", src/shell/strings/en.ts:10).
- Fix: `baseUrl: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE ?? 'https://api.metis.test'` (the env mechanism src/platform/mocks.ts:6 already uses); once the back-end exists, the home workspace comes from the shell contract or a /me call and HOME leaves shipped code.
- approach-changing: no, a one-line seam now, the contract change later.
💭 nit  The per-component .styles.ts split is forced by lint but adds no token safety
- key: eslint.config.js#styles-file-split
- Where: eslint.config.js:28-32 (StyleSheet banned outside *.styles.ts); eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js:2-4 (already checks every object in src, not only StyleSheet.create); src/design-system/Spinner.styles.ts:3-5 (a file for one constant whose comment says it exists only so every colour sits in a *.styles.ts file).
- Why: 42 .styles.ts files today, 8 of them 10 lines or fewer (Spinner 5, NotBuilt 8, tier 8, CategoryCard 8, Logo 9, ListNote 9, TileRow 10, WorkloadCard 10); plan C adds about ten per screen. Token safety comes from no-style-literals and inline style objects are already banned by the first selector (eslint.config.js:20-23), so the second file buys only a convention.
- Fix: delete the StyleSheet selector (eslint.config.js:28-32) and let `StyleSheet.create` sit at the bottom of the component file; keep the inline-object ban and no-style-literals. If the team keeps the split, name the trade-off: twice the files in exchange for one place to look.
- approach-changing: no, a lint relaxation; existing files can stay.
💭 nit  Platform forks for a single value (ponytail)

The default-file fallback is already relied on [Source: src/design-system/Select.tsx:17-19, the default file serves web beside Select.ios.tsx and Select.android.tsx]. Net: about -15 lines, -4 files.
- approach-changing: no.
